'''Robert George Bergman''' is an American chemist. He is Professor of the Graduate School and Gerald E. K. Branch Distinguished Professor Emeritus at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Robert G. Bergman {{!}} College of Chemistry|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/bergman|access-date=2021-05-14|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Born in [[Chicago]], Robert Bergman was the son of Joseph J. and Stella Bergman, née Horowitz.{{citation needed|date=January 2023|reason=existing citation do not mention date or place of birth}} In 1963 he graduated from [[Carleton College]] with a degree in chemistry. Under the supervision of [[Jerome A. Berson]], he received a PhD in 1966 from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]]. From 1966 to 1967 he was a NATO postdoctoral fellow at [[Ronald Breslow]]'s laboratory at [[Columbia University]], New York City.<ref name=":0" /> 

== Career ==
Bergman began his independent career at the [[California Institute of Technology]] in Pasadena where he was an [[Arthur Amos Noyes|Arthur Noyes]] Research Instructor (1967–1969), assistant professor (1969–1971), associate professor (1971–1973), and full professor (1973–1977).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert G. Bergman – Bergman Group|url=https://rgbgrp.cchem.berkeley.edu/rgbbio/|access-date=2021-05-14|language=en-US}}</ref> From 1977 to 2002, he was a chemistry professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and since 1978 has also been a researcher at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. In 2002 he was appointed Gerald E. K. Branch Distinguished Professor of Chemistry. Bergman transitioned to Emeritus status in 2016 and now holds to the titles of Professor of the Graduate School and Gerald E. K. Branch Distinguished Professor Emeritus.<ref name=":0" />

=== Research ===
Bergman works in the field of [[organic chemistry]]. He first investigated the reaction mechanisms of organic reactions at Caltech. He developed methods for the representation of very reactive molecules, for example 1,3-diradicals and vinyl cations. In 1972, he discovered the thermal cyclization of ''cis''-1,5-hexadiyne-3-ene to 1,4-dehydrobenzene-diradicals, now known as the [[Bergman cyclization]].<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Richard R. |last1=Jones |first2=Robert G. |last2=Bergman |title=p-Benzyne. Generation as an intermediate in a thermal isomerization reaction and trapping evidence for the 1,4-benzenediyl structure |journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] |volume=94 |issue=2 |year=1972 |pages=660–661 |doi=10.1021/ja00757a071|bibcode=1972JAChS..94..660J }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bergman|first=Robert G.|date=1973-01-01|title=Reactive 1,4-dehydroaromatics|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ar50061a004|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=6|issue=1|pages=25–31|doi=10.1021/ar50061a004|issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription}}</ref> This reaction later played a major role in understanding the mode of action of enediyne antitumor antibiotics.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lee|first1=May D.|last2=Ellestad|first2=George A.|last3=Borders|first3=Donald B.|date=1991-08-01|title=Calicheamicins: discovery, structure, chemistry, and interaction with DNA|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ar00008a003|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=24|issue=8|pages=235–243|doi=10.1021/ar00008a003|issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nicolaou|first1=K. C.|last2=Dai|first2=W.-M.|date=1991|title=Chemistry and Biology of the Enediyne Anticancer Antibiotics|url=https://www.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.199113873|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|language=en|volume=30|issue=11|pages=1387–1416|doi=10.1002/anie.199113873|issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Since the mid-1970s, Bergman has also been working in the field of [[organometallic chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Chirik|first=Paul J.|date=2017-03-13|title=Introduction to the Virtual Issue Honoring Robert Bergman's 2017 Wolf Prize in Chemistry|journal=Organometallics|volume=36|issue=5|pages=957–959|doi=10.1021/acs.organomet.7b00134|issn=0276-7333|doi-access=free}}</ref> He contributed to the synthesis and reaction of organometallic complexes and investigated organometallic compounds with metal-oxygen and metal-nitrogen bonds. He also discovered the first soluble organometallic complexes of the transition metals, to which the addition of a saturated hydrocarbon (C-H activation, C-H insertion) succeeded.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Andrew H. |last1=Janowicz |first2=Robert G. |last2=Bergman |title=Carbon-hydrogen activation in completely saturated hydrocarbons: direct observation of M + R-H .fwdarw. M(R)(H) |journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] |volume=104 |issue=1 |year=1982 |pages=352–354 |doi=10.1021/ja00365a091|bibcode=1982JAChS.104..352J }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=James K. |last1=Hoyano |first2=William A. G. |last2=Graham |title=Oxidative addition of the carbon hydrogen-bonds of neopentane and cyclohexane to a photochemically generated iridium(I) complex |journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] |volume=104 |issue=13 |year=1982 |pages=3723–3725 |doi=10.1021/ja00377a032|bibcode=1982JAChS.104.3723H }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Since June 17, 1965, Bergman has been married. The Bergmans have two sons.{{cn|date=May 2022}}
